title: fix(docker): Self-Heal Stale Docker Desktop Bind Mounts
description: Clears Docker Desktop's dangling WSL bind-mount staging entries before starting containers, retries a start once when the engine reports one, and removes a worktree's entries when it is torn down.

test_plan.description: A single-file bind mount whose host file is replaced no longer breaks the next container start
steps: On a Docker Desktop + WSL host, start a project that bind-mounts a single file (e.g. ./docker/php/local.ini:/usr/local/etc/php/conf.d/local.ini) with `ngramx up`
Replace that file on the host so its inode changes: `git checkout <other-branch> -- docker/php/local.ini`, or `mv local.ini x && cp x local.ini`
Confirm the staged mount is now dead: `awk '/docker-desktop-bind-mounts/ && $4 ~ /deleted/ {print $4, $5}' /proc/self/mountinfo`
Expect it to report 'Clearing N stale Docker Desktop bind mount(s)…' and start cleanly, rather than failing with 'error mounting … no such file or directory'
On a host where sudo needs a password and there is no TTY, expect the exact `sudo umount …` command to be printed instead of a hang

test_plan.description: Removing a worktree does not leave staged mounts behind for the next worktree at that path
steps: Create a worktree environment: `ngramx worktree gig-1234`
Note the staged mounts for it: `grep <worktree path> /proc/self/mountinfo`
Expect no staging entries to remain for that worktree path
Recreate the same worktree and confirm its containers start first time
Occupy a port the project needs, then run `ngramx up`
Expect the usual port-conflict handling and error — no stale-mount messaging, no silent retry
